audit_question: After resolving the recurring current-core handle/fit boundary, does a materially different cohort focused on tether constructions and anchor-side installation remain predominantly A/B without a comparable recurring C/D seam?
decision: The cohort is narrowly A/B-majority by count, but the three C cases recur independently across Milwaukee, FallTech and Ergodyne and all expose the same anchor-side installation-eligibility gap. Do not declare semantic saturation yet. Treat one conservative AnchorAttachment installation/binding slice as the remaining high-value model seam; the five tether B cases are catalogue-throughput work and should not drive new core vocabulary.

products.name: 35 lb. Medium Duty Elasticated Tool Tether
observed_public_facts: swivel aluminum twist-locking carabiner on one end
choker web loop on the other end
core_fit: loop endpoint with evidence-bound choking/cinch engagement
products.portability_gap: Safewaze requires acquisition/extraction and careful preservation of the choker mechanism. The observed endpoint, connector, length and capacity facts fit existing manufacturer-neutral tether primitives.

products.name: 5 lb. Coil Tool Tether
observed_public_facts: two twist-lock aluminum carabiners, one at each end
products.portability_gap: The coil construction is descriptive rather than a new recommendation primitive. Safewaze ingestion is missing, while the two carabiner endpoints, length range and capacity already fit the neutral core.

products.name: 5Lbs 50 in. Retractable Tool Lanyard
core_fit: manufacturer-declared compatibility can remain separately evidence-bound
products.portability_gap: The existing Milwaukee adapter is tool-focused and does not onboard this tether family. Quick-Connect branding must not create SKU-pair logic, but the physical tether facts fit existing endpoint, connector, length and capacity semantics.

products.name: 5 lb Retractable Tool Tether, Carabiner Style
observed_public_facts: stainless-steel screw-gate connector at each end
products.portability_gap: Guardian acquisition/extraction is the missing layer. The retractable construction and dual screw-gate endpoint facts require no new downstream compatibility or recommendation primitive.

products.name: 15 lb Tool Tether with dual aluminum twist-lock carabiners, 36 in
observed_public_facts: captive eye pins keep the carabiners attached to the tether
core_fit: connector captive-eye construction as connector evidence rather than tool-feature captivity
products.portability_gap: The current FallTech extractor is intentionally narrow around a steel-carabiner plus cinch-loop heading. Extending it to dual aluminum twist-lock endpoints is vendor ingestion work over existing neutral tether and connector primitives.

products.name: 50lbs Anchor Strap
observed_public_facts: strap loop securely wraps around beams and rails
oversized D-ring holds up to five carabiners
core_fit: AnchorPathOption once a valid installed path is already resolved
required_core_changes: add a reusable evidence-backed AnchorAttachment installation eligibility and concrete anchor-feature binding layer so beam/rail installation is proven rather than assumed when an AnchorPathOption is supplied
products.portability_gap: The core can represent the attachment component and the D-ring it provides to the tether, but candidate generation consumes an already-resolved AnchorPathOption. It cannot currently prove from manufacturer evidence that this strap is installable on the selected beam or rail without an external pre-resolution step.

products.name: Waist Belt Cinch Anchor Attachment
observed_public_facts: fits most full-body harness belts and other small-diameter anchorage locations
steel D-ring provides the tool-tether connection point
core_fit: AnchorPathOption once a valid installed path is already resolved
required_core_changes: add the same generic AnchorAttachment installation eligibility and selected anchor-feature binding seam, preserving choke-on method and anchor-target evidence without assuming every belt or small structure is valid
products.portability_gap: This independently repeats Milwaukee's downstream gap with a different installation method and target wording: the installed anchor path can be represented after selection, but the catalogue/runtime core cannot yet derive and prove that installation against a concrete belt or anchorage feature.

products.name: Anchor Strap Belt Loop Attachment for Tool Tethering
observed_public_facts: enclosed loop threads over belts or fall-protection harnesses
manufacturer instructions require an open-ended primary anchor that can be refastened and secured against slide-off
steel D-ring provides the lanyard attachment point
fits belts and harnesses up to 3 inches and carries a 5 lb / 2.3 kg maximum load
core_fit: AnchorPathOption once a valid installed path is already resolved
required_core_changes: add the recurring AnchorAttachment installation eligibility/binding seam with enough manufacturer-neutral anchor-feature vocabulary to distinguish evidence such as an open-ended refastenable belt from an arbitrary anchor target; preserve the 3 inch statement as an explicit installation bound rather than generic fit inference
products.portability_gap: The product makes the missing pre-AnchorPath layer explicit. Existing candidate generation can consume its D-ring and component only after a valid installed anchor path has somehow been chosen; there is no generic evidence-backed mechanism equivalent to ToolAttachment eligibility for proving the selected primary anchor is installable.
